brief.situation: You maintain overdue_report.py for the Northfield Library District (fictional). It marks overdue loans whose patron is blocked so the hold desk handles them, and writes the notice file the nine branches use when they open at 07:00. Since Thursday it takes 95 minutes instead of 3. It is 05:40 and tonight's file is not written yet.
handover: A colleague's note: 'Probably needs more cores. Try multiprocessing?'
yesterday_expected.csv is last night's checked output, kept for testing.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: open or profile something, run a query, a check or a test, change the code or the model, or ship the result. A cell marked with a pencil can be changed by picking a value. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
The console shows what is open, its flags, charts, tables and code, and the result of each step. 'Read the console' reads it aloud, and every chart can be shown as a table.
Shipping is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

parts.criteria: Names the membership test inside is_blocked: a list scanned once per loan, which grew from 3,100 to 26,480 IDs on Thursday.
parts.modelAnswer: patron_id in blocked scans a list; 40,212 loans times 26,480 IDs. The list grew eightfold on Thursday.

parts.label: How you found it
parts.criteria: Measured before changing anything: cProfile sorted by cumulative time (is_blocked 97%, tottime equal to cumtime) or timeit on the call.
parts.modelAnswer: cProfile on a sample: is_blocked was 4.58 of 4.71 s, all of it in the function itself; timeit put one check at 2.3 ms.

parts.label: Why the change works and how you know
parts.criteria: A set makes the membership test O(1) on average; the output was diffed against a known good file before sending. More processes, a cache on a list argument, or skipping the check do not fix it.
parts.modelAnswer: blocked = {...} turns each check into a hash lookup; the job ran in 2 min and the diff against yesterday's output was empty.

scoring.modelReasoning: Profile before optimizing: cProfile sorted by cumulative time shows is_blocked taking 97% of the run, and its time is its own, so the cost is the membership test against a list (O(n) per check in CPython). The blocked list grew from 3,100 to 26,480 IDs on Thursday, which is exactly when the run time jumped. Building it once as a set (O(1) average) brings the job to 2 minutes. More processes divide the same quadratic work; lru_cache cannot hash a list argument; skipping the check is fast and wrong. Diffing against yesterday's checked output proves the change kept the result.
